recent_context.fact: Press Forward South Florida, an initiative fueled in part by The Miami Foundation, announced grants to more than a dozen newsrooms and partnerships serving Broward, Miami-Dade and Monroe counties.
The Miami Foundation partnered with McDermott Will & Schulte to provide pro bono legal counsel to 17 Miami nonprofits, resulting in 398 hours of service valued at more than $500,000.

The Miami Foundation committed $100,000 in rapid-response support for Spanish-language coverage through elTOQUE and City of Miami coverage through The Florida Trib in partnership with the Coconut Grove Spotlight.
Press Forward South Florida awarded Newsroom Collaboration grants including $100,000 to WLRN and $100,000 to Florida International University's Lee Caplin School of Journalism & Media.

The Miami Foundation commissioned and unveiled South Dade Community Needs and Nonprofit Funding Landscape, which analyzed more than 1,400 grants to 262 South Dade nonprofits and included interviews with 19 community leaders, providers and advocates.

Inspired directly by the Foundation-commissioned report, Amazon announced a $1 million investment in 13 South Dade nonprofit organizations to strengthen their capacity and deepen their community impact.
The Miami Foundation awarded scholarships totaling $3.45 million to 969 students this year.
The Jorge M. Pérez Family Foundation at The Miami Foundation announced a $720,000 investment in Miami-Dade County's nonprofit arts sector through its CreARTE grant program.
The Miami Foundation activates its Disaster Resilience Fund with foundations and philanthropists to support disaster preparedness and equitable long-term recovery efforts.

During Florida's 2021 legislative session, Senator Ileana Garcia and State Representative Nick Duran led a successful bipartisan effort to create the Biscayne Bay specialty license plate, with plate-sale revenue designated to preserve and restore Biscayne Bay.
In 2021, Miami-Dade County received a challenge grant offer from the Adrienne Arsht-Rockefeller Foundation Resilience Center to fast start an extreme heat initiative under the Resilient305 program.
The Miami Disaster Resilience Fund is investing $135,000 in resilience hubs and community-based organizations strengthening preparedness across Miami-Dade County.
